newsitem.title: FRANCE: C.National agrees no job cuts for 15 mths.
newsitem.headline: C.National agrees no job cuts for 15 mths.

text.p: The chairman of French bank Credit National has agreed that there will be no compulsory redundancies for 15 months from January 1, 1997.

A Credit National spokesman told Reuters on Friday that chairman Emmanuel Rodocanachi made the announcement on Thursday after a meeting with unions produced two agreements relating to the merger of Credit National and the Banque Francaise du Commerce Exterieur (BFCE).
Eventually, the merger will lead to the loss of 600 permanent jobs.
Rodocanachi also announced that a planned voluntary redundancy programme would not be implemented in the first quarter of 1997.
The labour agreement, signed by all the bank unions, includes an undertaking to drop legal action opposing the merger of the two trading rooms.
After consultations, the smaller Credit National trading room will transfer to the BFCE's larger installation on Boulevard Haussmann, central Paris, by the end of the year.
The two banks eventually will integrate their domestic banking operations and computer systems.
